interview.hardest_part: Precise first-person climbing: PEAK requires chaining short stamina-limited climbs, grabbing ledges, and aiming at specific handholds with continuous mouse movement, but I only get 1-second discrete inputs from a single static screenshot with no depth or motion feedback, so lining up a grab and knowing when to release is extremely hard.
interview.likely_failure: Most likely I fail on the very first vertical obstacle above the beach: I misjudge the distance to a ledge, waste stamina on failed grabs or a fall, and get stuck or downed before reaching even 10 m, or I fail to find the route out of the airport/shore area at all.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Stamina regenerates when standing on solid ground so I can attempt climbs repeatedly; the 10 m/25 m milestones are cumulative-height checkpoints that can be reached by small safe hops; forgiving ledge grabs and the 'hand' assist mean slow, cautious progress is still possible; deterministic arrow-key look aliases let me aim the camera reliably in fixed increments.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Stamina drain and falling damage punish mistimed inputs; the discrete 1 s action steps make fine adjustments and mid-air corrections nearly impossible; limited view from a single screenshot hides the route and handhold geometry; the rotating daily island prevents memorizing layouts across attempts; the 2-attempt cap and 6-hour wall-clock budget sharply limit how much trial-and-error learning I can do, and later regions (ALPINE, CALDERA) demand sustained precision far beyond what blind 1 s inputs support.
